units.scenario: B is Yamada-sensei, whom Nam meets again after a long break. Nam must greet him for the time of day, ask how he is, thank him, apologise and say goodbye politely. Then B is the manager of the restaurant where she works, and Nam must use the right phrases for leaving work before others and saying good night.

B is Yamada-sensei, checking Nam's hiragana in class. Nam must read simple hiragana words aloud — seafood and snacks on a menu (たこ, いか, すし, おかし) and things around her (かさ, いす, くつ) — and thank him or say sorry when he corrects her.

B is a Japanese guest at a small welcome party. Nam must introduce herself (her name, that she is Thai, from Bangkok and a university student, and which languages she speaks), ask his name and whether he speaks English or Thai, then introduce her new friend Yuki to him and ask what he does.
B is Yuki, eating at a Japanese restaurant in Bangkok with Nam. Nam must read the dishes on the hiragana menu aloud (さしみ, やきとり, すきやき, もち), ask what one dish is and order with おねがいします.

B is a fruit seller at a market stall, and later Yamada-sensei taking the class register. Nam must ask for fruit and say how many she wants (one to ten), count along with the seller, and then tell the teacher her age, her year at university and her number on the class list.

B is Yuki, having lunch with Nam at a small restaurant. Nam must say what she will eat and drink, order cold drinks, say which food and fruit she likes and how things taste (sweet, spicy, salty), and say いただきます and ごちそうさまでした.
B is Yuki. Nam must ask and say what colour things are — fruit, shoes, the Thai and Japanese flags, a traffic light — say which colours she likes, and say what the two flags have in common.
B is Yuki. Nam must say which animals she likes or dislikes (pets, farm, zoo and sea animals), describe them as cute, strong or weak, say whether they swim or fly, and ask which animals are Japanese.

B is Yuki, visiting Bangkok. Nam must talk about today's and tomorrow's weather (sunny, rain, a storm), say how hot it is and give the temperature, compare Thai weather with the Japanese seasons, and ask which season and seasonal flowers Yuki likes.

B is Yuki, looking at photos with Nam. Nam must say who the people are (Yamada-sensei and his child, men, women, children), describe what they are like and how they look (kind, funny, serious, young, thin, short hair, glasses), and ask Yuki about her own teacher and famous Japanese manga artists.
B is Yuki. Nam must say what she loves, likes, doesn't like much or hates — animals, music, films, sports and food — ask what Yuki likes, and give reasons with どうして and から.

B is Yuki, who tells Nam about her busy, surprising day. Nam must react naturally (ほんとうですか, へえ, なるほど, たいへんですね), say how she feels (tired, hungry, bored or having fun) and answer Yuki's compliment on her Japanese modestly (まだまだです).

B is Yuki, talking with Nam about a day out in nature. Nam must say whether she likes the sea or the mountains, name what can be seen there (islands, waterfalls, the sunset, mushrooms), say what she likes doing outdoors (walking, swimming, fishing, taking photos) and ask about Yuki's favourite places.

B is Yamada-sensei in Nam's Japanese class. Nam must say whether she understands, ask him to say a word again slowly, ask what it means, explain the meaning of a Thai word, ask for a pencil and say which homework questions were difficult.

B is Yuki, telling Nam about Japanese culture. Nam must say what she likes or finds interesting — public baths, castles and torii gates, lucky charms, summer festivals, sumo and ninja — and compare manners such as taking off shoes and queueing quietly with Thailand.

B is Yuki's mother, welcoming Nam to the family's home in Japan at New Year. Nam must call at the door and greet her politely (ごめんください, おじゃまします), wish her a happy New Year, give her a small present modestly, politely decline a drink and say goodbye properly (おじゃましました).

B is Yuki, who has sent Nam a hiragana postcard from Kyoto. Nam must read the postcard and Japanese city names aloud (とうきょう, きょうと, ほっかいどう), getting voiced sounds, っ, small ゃゅょ and long vowels right, and tell Yuki what she reads in Japanese.

B is Yuki. Nam must read katakana aloud — country names and a poster for a Thai festival in Tokyo — say which countries her friends come from, and show Yuki how Thai places and dishes are written in katakana (バンコク, チェンマイ, トムヤムクン).
B is Yuki. Nam must tell the time, say when her classes start and end and on which days, give her birthday, talk about yesterday and the day after tomorrow, and fix a date to meet.

B is a shop assistant at a bag shop. Nam must point at bags near and far (この, その, あの), ask the prices and whether there are other colours, say when something is a bit expensive, choose one and pay by card or cash.

B is a passer-by, and later a station attendant. Nam must ask where places are (a park, a library, the station), understand directions (straight on, left, right, next to, in front of, near, far), and ask which platform to use, where to change trains and where to get off.

B is Yuki. Nam must describe her daily routine (when she gets up and goes to bed, her Saturday job at a restaurant, how often she does things), introduce her family in Bangkok — her parents, both teachers, and her younger sister Fah — and ask about Yuki's older brother.

B is a shop assistant at a clothes shop. Before her winter trip to Hokkaido, Nam must ask for a warm coat, ask for another colour and a slightly bigger size (M or L), try it on in the fitting room and decide which one to buy.

B is Yuki, visiting Nam's family home in Bangkok for the first time. Nam must show her the rooms and the garden, say what is in each room and where things are (on, under, behind), describe her own room and say where the family's cat is.

B is a convenience-store clerk. Nam must find what she wants for lunch (a bento, onigiri, bread, drinks), say how many with the right counters (こ, ほん, まい), answer whether to heat the bento and whether she needs chopsticks or a spoon, and pay.

B is a waiter at a café where Nam is eating with Yuki. Nam must say how many they are, ask for the menu, order coffee and a lunch set, ask for a fork and napkins, and ask for the bill so they can pay together.

B is Yuki's mother answering the phone at the Tanaka home in Japan, and later Yuki herself. Nam must say who she is, ask for Yuki, say she will call back later and give her mobile number digit by digit; then she and Yuki agree on a time for a video call, keeping the two-hour time difference in mind.

B is Yuki, and then a pharmacist. Nam must say she feels unwell and where it hurts, say she has a cold and keeps sneezing, ask the pharmacist for cold medicine and how many times a day to take it, and say she will stay home from class until she gets better.

B is Yuki, looking at a calendar with Nam. Nam must talk about this week, this month and next year, ask when Japanese holidays such as Golden Week and Obon are, give her birthday, and say where she wants to go and what she wants to do in the summer holidays (〜たいです).

B is Yuki. Nam must say what she does in her free time (films, music, sports, going out), say which sports she is good or bad at, ask Yuki the same, and tell her what she did last weekend and how it was (〜ました).

B is a receptionist at a hotel in Kyoto, and later Yuki. Nam must ask for a single room for two nights, ask for an extra blanket and when the museum opens and closes, and afterwards tell Yuki what she did, which souvenirs she bought for whom and how she got home (〜ました).

B is a station attendant, and then a police officer at a こうばん, during Nam's trip in Japan. Nam must say she left her wallet on the train and roughly when, describe the wallet and what is inside, and thank him when it is found.

B is Yuki, who is recruiting new members for the university dance club. Nam must talk about her hobbies, say what she is good or bad at and what she can and cannot do — such as playing the guitar, swimming or skiing — and decide whether to join.
B is a doctor at a clinic near the university. Nam must say where it hurts and since when, describe the symptoms, and check how and when to take the medicine.
B is Yamada-sensei in an advising session. Nam must talk about her major, compare her favourite and most difficult subjects, and say what job she wants after graduating.
B is Yuki on the phone. Nam must invite Yuki to an event, agree on the day, time and meeting place, and politely turn down one of Yuki's suggestions.
B is the manager of Nam's student dormitory on moving-in day. Nam must ask for help and information, ask permission (cooking late, having a guest) and check which dormitory rules must be followed.

B is Yuki at a café after the winter holidays. Nam must describe her trip to Hokkaido (what it was like and what she did there, in order) and ask and answer questions about experiences, such as whether Yuki has ever been to Chiang Mai.
B is Yuki chatting with Nam over lunch. Nam must switch to plain (casual) forms to talk about plans and yesterday, ask questions with 〜の？ and explain things with 〜んだ.
B is Yuki planning a weekend outing with Nam. Nam must check the weather forecast with her, say what the weather may be like and suggest a plan for both rain and sunshine.

B is Yuki, who is waiting with Nam for a friend at a busy station and then helps Nam pick an outfit for a party. Nam must describe what people are wearing and what they look like, and say what is too flashy, too plain or too tight.
B is Yuki, who wants to learn to cook a Thai dish. Nam must name the ingredients, explain the steps in order and give tips (what to get ready first, what not to add, how to tell when it is done).
B is the manager of a convenience store interviewing Nam for a part-time job. Nam must answer questions about experience and free days, and ask about pay, shifts and the rules.
B is a clerk at a post office counter. Nam must send a parcel to Thailand, choose how to send it, fill in the form and ask about the price and how long delivery takes.

B is Yuki, who wants to start exercising. Nam must talk about the sports she plays or watches, compare them, describe a match result and give advice on how to start (what is better to do and not to do).
B is Yuki, who is curious about Thai festivals. Nam must explain a Thai festival (when it is held and what people do), ask about a Japanese summer festival and agree to go together.
B is Yuki helping Nam choose a present. Nam must talk about presents she has given and received, ask Yuki's advice on what to give Yamada-sensei, and thank someone properly for a gift.
B is a clerk at a mobile phone shop. Nam must say what she needs from a new phone and plan, ask how to set it up, and compare which plan is easier to use and cheaper.

B is Yamada-sensei leading a class discussion about student life. Nam must give and explain an opinion on topics such as part-time jobs for students and pass on a message from Yuki, who is absent today.
B is Yuki planning a spring-break trip with Nam. Nam must suggest where to go, say what she intends to do there, and agree on transport, budget and schedule.
B is the receptionist at a ryokan. Nam must check in, ask about meals, the baths and check-out time, and ask what to do about a problem in the room.
B is a station attendant at a ticket office. Nam has missed a connection because of a delay and must ask about refunds, the next express or local train and seat options, and decide what to do.
B is Yamada-sensei in a progress interview before the JLPT. Nam must say what she can and cannot do in Japanese now, describe how her skills have changed, and ask for advice on how to study.
B is Yuki, whose laptop has broken just before a deadline. Nam must offer help, tell her what friends have done for her before, and politely ask Yuki for a favour in return.
B is Yuki, who looks tired and worried before a job interview. Nam must notice how she seems, ask what is wrong, share her own feelings and cheer her up.
B is Yuki chatting about what is going on around campus. Nam must pass on news she heard and say where she heard it, guess what is happening from what she can see, and react naturally to Yuki's news.
B is an estate agent. Nam must describe the room she wants (rent, distance from the station, sunlight), ask about conditions such as the deposit and contract, and arrange a viewing.

B is a neighbour who comes to complain politely that Nam put rubbish out on the wrong day. Nam must apologise, ask about the rules (which day, which bag) and politely raise a problem of her own (noise from upstairs).
B is a waiter at a busy izakaya. Nam is ordering for a group and must ask for recommendations, order the right quantities, ask for a dish to be made less spicy, and sort out the bill.
B is a customer-service operator on the phone. Nam's online order arrived damaged and in the wrong colour; Nam must explain the problem and choose between a refund and an exchange.
B is Yuki, whose family has a dog and who wants to adopt a cat. Nam must describe animals and how they behave, talk about nature in Thailand, and explain how things have changed over the years.
B is Yuki, who has started dating someone and asks Nam for advice. Nam must ask how things are going, share her own hopes and give gentle advice about a disagreement.

B is a staff member at the city disaster-prevention centre during a drill. Nam must ask what to do if an earthquake happens, check where the evacuation site is, and confirm what to keep ready at home.
B is Yamada-sensei in an end-of-year interview. Nam must explain what she wanted to be as a child, what she plans to do after her exchange year ends, and what she is already doing towards that goal.
B is a nurse at the university health check. Nam must describe her daily habits (sleep, meals, exercise), understand the nurse's advice and say what she will try to do or avoid from now on.
B is Yuki preparing a presentation on plastic waste in Thailand and Japan. Nam must explain causes and effects, say who is affected and how, and propose what individuals can do.
B is Yuki discussing the news over coffee. Nam must summarise a story she read (who did what to whom), report what people are saying about it and give her own view.

B is Yamada-sensei, who is curious about schools in Thailand. Nam must describe what teachers make students do, what students are and aren't allowed to do, and give an opinion on what schools should do.

B is a businessman staying at the hotel where Nam works part-time at the front desk. Nam must greet him, ask what he would like using honorific forms, explain the hotel services and give polite instructions.
B is a staff member of a client company calling Nam's office, where Nam is an intern. Nam must introduce herself humbly, explain that the manager is out, take a message and arrange a visit.

B is an interviewer at a Japanese company's office in Bangkok. Nam must explain why she applied, talk about what she learned through part-time work and study, and say what role she could play in the company.
B is Yuki, who always runs out of money before payday. Nam must compare spending habits, complain about prices and suggest ways to save money and keep a budget.

B is an elderly neighbour who has just been given her first smartphone by her children. Nam must explain step by step how to send a message and make a video call, warn her what not to do, and chat about how technology has changed life.
B is a Japanese businessman about to be posted to Bangkok. Nam must compare work culture, food, transport and climate in the two countries, and explain that not all Thai people are the same.

B is a Japanese exchange student who is going to Thailand next month. Nam must explain Thai manners (temples, monks, the head and feet), say what visitors should not do, and react to the Japanese customs the student describes.
B is Yuki at an izakaya after a long week. Nam must tell a funny or scary thing that happened to her, in order and with how she felt, and react to Yuki's own story.
B is Yuki, who is upset because Nam did not answer her messages for three days. Nam must explain what happened, clear up the misunderstanding and make up with her.

B is a Japanese tourist visiting Ayutthaya, where Nam is a volunteer guide. Nam must explain when and by whom the temples were built, what happened in history, and recommend a route and the best time to visit.

B is Yuki, who is writing a report on Thai food culture. Nam must explain how Thai people eat (sharing dishes, street food, eating little and often), compare this with Japanese habits and talk about her own eating habits.
B is a clerk at the ward office. Nam has just moved and must register her new address, ask which documents are needed, and understand what has to be done before what.

B is Yuki, who now works for a company and complains about overtime. Nam must ask about her working conditions, compare working styles in Thailand and Japan, and suggest realistic ways to balance work and life.
B is Yamada-sensei, whose mother now needs care. Nam must ask about his situation, explain how families care for older people in Thailand, and discuss what society should do.
B is Yuki, whose teenage cousin is being bullied online. Nam must discuss the risks of social media, give advice on privacy and online safety, and suggest what the family can do.

B is a staff member at the city's international centre interviewing Nam for its newsletter. Nam must describe the difficulties foreign residents face, what has helped them, and what Japanese society could do better.

B is Yuki, who doubts that the new Thai café near the station where Nam has started working part-time will succeed. Nam must explain the manager's idea, the budget and the risks, and answer Yuki's doubts with examples.

B is Yamada-sensei chairing a seminar where Nam presents survey results on how students use their smartphones. Nam must structure the talk, explain the data, define key terms and answer a question from the audience.

B is a Japanese classmate on the opposing side of a class debate about whether university should be free. Nam must state her position, acknowledge his good points and argue back politely with examples.

B is a Japanese high-school student who has to write a science report. Nam must explain a discovery, describe how the research was done and discuss both the benefits and the risks of a new technology.
B is Yuki after watching a film with Nam. Nam must summarise the story without spoiling the ending, give her impression of the acting and music, and recommend a Thai film or novel to her.

B is a Japanese journalist interviewing Nam about how young Thais see Japan. Nam must talk about Japanese companies and culture in Thailand, give examples from her own life and explain why the relationship matters.
B is the leader of a volunteer group at a local international festival. Nam must offer to help, ask what tasks there are and when, and explain why she wants to volunteer.

B is Yuki at a shrine festival, where she buys an omikuji fortune with Nam. Nam must compare superstitions in Thailand and Japan, explain lucky and unlucky numbers and colours, and say how far she believes in them.

B is Yuki, who is thinking of moving to her grandparents' village and working remotely. Nam must compare city and country life, discuss the problems of shrinking villages and help her weigh up the pros and cons.

B is a Thai student who has just arrived in Japan and asks Nam for advice. Nam must talk about her own failures and what she learned from them, and give practical advice with examples from experience.

B is Nam's manager at the travel agency in Japan where she works, checking a draft email Nam wrote to a client. Nam must explain the purpose of the email, choose the right set phrases and fix expressions that are too casual.

B is Yamada-sensei helping Nam prepare a short speech for the farewell party his Japanese class is holding before she returns to Thailand. Nam must thank people properly, look back on her time in Japan and express wishes for the future in formal Japanese.
